title: Orbit train: weekly convergence + gated RCs with annotated changelog automation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Replace the ad-hoc weekly cut process with a deterministic 'orbit' cadence that produces a rollbackable Release Candidate (RC) each Thursday at 16:00 UTC, an LTS promotion signal on release windows, and an annotated changelog that surfaces issue-level impact and migration notes. This ticket defines the gating criteria, RC tag format, automated changelog generation, and lightweight upgrade checks to reduce late-stage regressions.

Background: Our current weekly build process relies on manual tagging and post-hoc changelog compilation. That causes delays in shipping fixes, inconsistent upgrade notes for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments, and occasional surprises during LTS promotions. The orbit cadence must be deterministic, auditable, and provide machine-readable metadata for Console rollouts and SDK release notes.

Scope:
- Define RC tagging convention (orbit-YYYYMMDD-RC<N> and metadata annotations for backports, migration flags, and binary compatibility).
- Implement gating pipeline in CI: test matrix (smoke, e2e-canary, perf quick-check), flakiness threshold, and automatable human-in-the-loop approvals for security or infra-sensitive changes.
- Generate annotated changelog per RC with categories (fix, perf, breaking, migration), linked PRs, affected subsystems, and minimal upgrade instructions. Produce both human HTML/MD and machine-readable JSON for Console and release notes automation.
- Provide a rollback plan and automated revert PR template when RC fails post-cut.
- Integrate with Console: surface upcoming RCs on the Release page, expose rollout gates status, and attach changelog blobs.

Non-goals: full productized upgrade assistant (separate initiative), redesign of existing release-notes UI components beyond adding a changelog attachment.

Design decisions:
- RC cadence locked to weekly orbit to simplify customer expectations and reduce hotfix frequency.
- Use a three-tier gate: automated checks -> canary cluster smoke -> manual sign-off if any infra/security flags. Manual sign-off only required when flagged; otherwise pipeline can promote automatically to RC tag.
- Annotated changelogs created from PR labels and structured release notes in PR templates. For older PRs lacking labels, fall back to heuristic classification based on title and file paths.

Success criteria:
- Every weekly orbit produces an RC tag that includes a changelog JSON artifact and an HTML summary attached to the tag.
- Time-to-cut reduced to <15 minutes of manual overhead on release day for non-flagged weeks.
- Reduction in L0 regressions attributed to release process by 30% within two release cycles.
- Console surfaces RC status and changelog for each customer-facing release.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline produces an orbit RC tag and artifacts (changelog.json, changelog.md) automatically on successful gate
RC tag name follows convention orbit-YYYYMMDD-RC<#> and contains metadata fields: generated_by, gate_results, backports
Annotated changelog contains categorized entries with source PR links and migration notes where applicable
Console shows upcoming RC entries with pass/fail gate indicators and a link to the changelog artifact

notes: RC tag format decision: orbit-<date>-RCn (ex: orbit-20260312-RC1). Always increment RC number on same-day re-cuts.
Changelog JSON schema: version, date, generated_by, entries[] where entry contains type, title, pr, author, subsystem, migration_notes (optional).
Rollout gates documented in runbook: smoke timeout 10m, canary pass threshold 95% for success metrics, flakiness threshold 3 flaky tests -> mark for manual review.
Release window: LTS promotions gated to every 6th orbit; LTS candidate must have zero critical regressions and explicit PM approval.
